:::{#exm-pois-two-group-ci}
#### Confidence interval for a two-cohort rate ratio

In @exm-pois-two-group-mle,
$D_0 = 12$, $D_1 = 15$, and $\eb_1 = \logf{2} \approx 0.693$.
By @thm-pois-two-group-se:

$$
\ba
\ese{\eb_1}
&= \sqrt{\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15}}
&& \text{(two-group standard error formula)} \\
&= \sqrt{0.0833 + 0.0667}
&& \text{(evaluate each fraction)} \\
&= \sqrt{0.15}
&& \text{(add)} \\
&\approx 0.387
&& \text{(square root)}
\ea
$$

The Wald 95% confidence interval for $\b_1$ is then

$$
\ba
\eb_1 \pm 1.96 \cdot \ese{\eb_1}
&= 0.693 \pm 1.96 \cdot 0.387
&& \text{(substitute)} \\
&= 0.693 \pm 0.759
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= \sb{-0.066, 1.452}
&& \text{(add and subtract)}
\ea
$$

and exponentiating both endpoints gives a 95% confidence interval
for the rate ratio of
$\sb{\expf{-0.066}, \expf{1.452}} \approx \sb{0.94, 4.27}$.
The point estimate doubles the rate,
but with only 27 events in total the interval still includes 1.

R's `confint.default()`,
which computes Wald intervals from the observed information,
reproduces this interval:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
exp(confint.default(fit_two_cohorts, parm = "exposed"))
```

:::
